TunaStream needs to be running on the PC, on the same network as this device.
Answer a few questions and TunaReceive picks the right settings for this TV.

Over Bluetooth, Android only lets apps rumble controllers its own drivers understand. When it doesn\'t, no app can make that controller rumble in that mode. A different connection mode on the controller, or a USB adapter, may show up differently here.

This 8BitDo adapter is in its Xbox (PC) mode, probably from being plugged into a PC. To put it back in its Android mode, which also reports battery and motion: unplug it, wait 10 seconds, turn the controller off, plug the adapter back in here, then turn the controller on without holding any button.
During a stream, TunaReceive drives this itself, rumble included.
TunaReceive doesn\'t recognise this as a controller yet. Send these numbers to whoever maintains TunaReceive.
Android runs this controller, but can\'t rumble it. During a stream TunaReceive takes it over and rumbles it itself (needs controller firmware 1.03 or later).
Its firmware supports rumble through the adapter.

1. On your PC, install TunaStream and keep it running. Its icon sits by the clock.

2. Connect this device to the same network as the PC, by cable or 5 GHz Wi-Fi if you can.

3. Your PC appears here by itself. If it doesn't, choose Add PC Manually and type the address shown on TunaStream's home page.

4. Choose the PC. A PIN appears: on the PC, open TunaStream, go to the PIN page, enter it and press Send.

5. Choose a game. It opens on its own screen on the PC, sized for this TV.

The PC doesn't show up: check that TunaStream is running and both are on the same network (guest Wi-Fi usually blocks this). Or choose Add PC Manually and type the address from TunaStream's home page.

Pairing fails: enter the PIN on TunaStream's PIN page within a minute or so, then try again.

The picture stutters: in this PC's menu, choose Fit picture quality to this connection. A cable, or 5 GHz Wi-Fi, helps most. Picture quality and size also adjust themselves while you play; afterwards, How the last stream went in the PC's menu says what happened.

The TV feels slow to respond: turn on auto low latency mode (ALLM) in the TV's HDMI settings so it switches to game mode by itself, or choose its Game mode by hand.

No rumble: on the PC, open TunaStream's Troubleshooting page during a stream and press Rumble now. If the controller buzzes, the game needs its vibration turned on; if not, check Rumble in this app's Settings.

The game opens on the PC's monitor: update TunaStream from its home page; it moves the game onto the stream's screen.

More help is on TunaStream's Help page on the PC.
Fit picture quality to this connection

That\'s how fast %1$s can send to this device. A Picture quality of %2$d Mbps (you have %3$d) leaves room for the Wi-Fi to dip without the stream stuttering.
That\'s how fast %1$s can send to this device. It has room for a sharper picture: %2$d Mbps instead of %3$d.
%1$s is on Wi-Fi itself (signal %2$d%%), so every frame crosses the air twice. A network cable from the PC to the router would help more than any setting here.

Adjust picture quality to the Wi-Fi
Watches how each frame arrives. When the Wi-Fi is getting full, it softens the picture a little before anything stutters, then goes back to full quality.

When the Wi-Fi drops a long way, send a smaller picture and let the TV stretch it, which looks cleaner than a blocky full-size one. It goes back to full size by itself. Needs Adjust picture quality to the Wi-Fi.
Sending a smaller picture for 10 seconds. It should stay full-screen, look a little softer, then sharpen again.
Can\'t try that here. Turn on both Adjust options in Settings, and update TunaStream on the PC.
Wear the colour theme chosen in TunaStream on the PC. Turn off to pick one for this TV below.
Switch the TV to game mode
While a game is on screen, ask the TV to skip its picture processing, which takes away a lot of delay. The TV goes back to normal afterwards. Needs a TV with auto low latency mode (ALLM).
Smoother colour gradients and slightly better use of the Wi-Fi, without HDR. Turn off if games show a black or green picture.
If a stream drops mid-game, start it again automatically. The game keeps running on the PC meanwhile.
That stream had some trouble. Hold the select button on the PC and choose How the last stream went to see what happened.

Picture quality turned itself down for %1$s of %2$s to keep things smooth, going as low as %3$d Mbps (your setting is %4$d). If that happens often, a lower Picture quality in Settings gives a steadier picture.

This usually means the Wi-Fi couldn't keep up for a moment. Lower the Picture quality in Settings, or long-press your PC and choose Fit picture quality to this connection. A smaller picture size (1080p instead of 4K) helps the most.

Sending the wake-up signal. Its games open as soon as it answers, usually within 30 seconds.

Waking a PC from the TV needs, on the PC:
• Wake-on-LAN switched on in its BIOS or UEFI settings
• In Device Manager, its network adapter's Power Management: "Allow this device to wake the computer" and "Only allow a magic packet to wake the computer"
• A network cable: most PCs can't be woken over Wi-Fi
• Sleep rather than shut down, unless the PC can be woken from off (then switch off Windows' Fast startup)

Waking only works on the same home network as the PC.
TunaReceive runs controllers it drives itself (8BitDo\'s 2.4G adapter) all the time it\'s open, not just in a game, so they move around the menus too. Off: Android runs them outside a game.

The game closes, and anything not saved is lost. To stop watching but keep playing later, choose Leave.
